The second proofs through the general laws are therefore no longer named theorems. The connection is a docstring line, as the review proposed. No name OPENING's body cites was removed. `Law.lost_stays`, which the RO passages and the chapter cite, stays as a one-line case.

**Not done, and why (G8).** The decided counting laws of Counting (`counting_free`, `counting_under`, `premised_counting`, `counting_binds_iff`, `enclosure_bounds_change` and the enclosed and finite families) do not become corollaries of CensusCounts' counted forms. Only their forward direction, from the tally to every decided world, follows from a counted form: by `CountsHold.obey` at worlds with decidable activity, a proof already of about five lines. The converse cannot follow. The counted hypothesis quantifies over every world meeting the selection, the decided one only over worlds with decidable activity, so both converses need the witness queues and rings. So does `counting_binds_iff`'s forward direction.

Putting the counted forms below would need Counting to import Decidedness (there is no cycle) and CensusCounts' 41 theorems to be interleaved through Counting's 4,630 lines. `counting_under` alone has 11 dependents in Counting's binding sections, and 38 declarations depend on the twelve laws. That restructure would save the five-line forward proofs and no witness. A shared witness lemma (B11's one census table), from which both converses are short, is the compression this item needs. It changes no statement and belongs with B11.
